title: Taifa of Carmona
capsule: The Taifa of Carmona was a Berber kingdom established by the Birzalid (Banu Birzal) clan of the Zenata confederation following the disintegration of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba after 1009. The taifa controlled the town of Carmona (modern Seville province) and its surrounding territory; it existed in two phases, the first ending when the Taifa of Seville under the Abbadid dynasty absorbed it around 1066, and a second brief episode roughly 1143–1150 under the Darddusid dynasty before the Almohad Caliphate consolidated Al-Andalus. The polity was minor in scale but exemplifies the fragmentation of Andalusian political authority that invited both Almoravid and Almohad intervention.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of this minor taifa is poorly documented; Carmona itself is certain as the capital but the precise boundaries of its hinterland control are reconstructed from general accounts of the taifa period rather than specific surveys.
